content.title: About
content.content: Lobster salad is a dish featuring cubed lobster meat combined with vegetables, herbs, and a light dressing made from mayonnaise or yogurt. It offers a delicate sea flavor, a hint of sweetness, and a refreshing texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lobster is considered a delicacy and is often served in fine‑dining restaurants.
Lobster meat is high in protein and contains all essential amino acids.
The classic lobster salad originated in New England in the early 20th century.
Traditional recipes often add hard‑boiled eggs, celery, and red onion for color and contrast.
Lobsters can be wild‑caught or farm‑raised; both provide the characteristic sweet flavor.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Lobster provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many seafoods, lobster contains very little saturated fat, making the salad a light option.

items.title: Source of zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are important for immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Lobster supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, aiding energy metabolism.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Small amounts of EPA and DHA support heart and brain health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to lobster.

items.title: High cost
items.content: Lobster is an expensive ingredient, which can limit frequent consumption.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: While low in fat, lobster does contain cholesterol, so people with high cholesterol should watch portions.

items.title: Potential contamination
items.content: Lobsters harvested from polluted waters may contain heavy metals; choose reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve lobster salad chilled, often on individual plates or atop lettuce leaves. Garnish with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, and a drizzle of olive oil. It pairs well with crusty bread or crackers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared lobster salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, keep the lobster meat, vegetables, and dressing separate to prevent sogginess.
